bugs.title: Series metadata validation is too strict/brittle — fix root cause (prompt ambiguity) and make validator recoverable (safe auto-correct of durable-request fields, clearer errors for ambiguous ones); do NOT just delete the safety check
bugs.notes: Verified a prior session's pushed commits a51204d/4ea7cdd/d8e15bd/7ca0135 constitute a complete, correct fix. Root cause: prompt.py SERIES_DIRECTIVE now states current part unambiguously and forbids copying part numbers from continuity text; series.js buildSeriesContext emits "Prior events (Part N):" instead of bare "Part N:"; fallback in prompt.py line ~1322 also reworded; series_id restated next to the production.json field spec. Recoverable failure: new pipeline/stage_b/series_reconcile.py auto-corrects series_id/part/start_seconds (both nested and flat shapes) from the durable stage-a-request.json with a logged change list, wired into stage-b.yml before the residual hard cross-check; end_seconds and non-metadata fields are never auto-corrected and still hard-fail with the expected value in the error. Tests: 42 passed across test_series.py, test_stage_b_series_reconcile.py, test_plan_cross_validation.py, covering wrong-part auto-correct (2a), non-series job untouched (2b), correct plan untouched (2c). The 13 failures elsewhere in pipeline/tests are pre-existing environment issues (cv2 CascadeClassifier stub, stage_a network, cleanup timing) in modules untouched by this fix — not regressions.

bugs.title: "Start next part" button (callback_data task:next:<label>) has no handler — dead callback in bot/src
bugs.notes: DEAD CALLBACK CLAIM REFUTED BY ACTUAL CODE: handleTaskCallback in bot/src/index.js contains "if (action === 'next') return startNextSeriesPart(env, chatId, label, messageId);" — the task:next:<label> button emitted by runtime.js is fully routed. startNextSeriesPart (index.js ~1394) reuses the canonical continuation logic: manualSeriesContinuation(status, request, plan) -> nextPartJobId -> nextPartRequestBody, with a duplicate-dispatch guard (existing stage-a-request/status check), writes queued status with full series block, dispatches Stage A, assigns a FRESH label via ensureTaskLabel, and renders a view whose only action opens the NEW part (task:open:<nextLabel>) — it never leaves the user on the completed prior part. Verified by reading the full dispatch table (all task: prefixes) and the handler body end-to-end. Confusion likely stems from stale git history: an older sweep used bug-57/58 ids for unrelated issues (status.series sync / deploy alerts), so earlier session notes were misleading. No code change needed. Bot suite: 122/122 pass after npm ci.

bugs.title: "Copy prompt" after starting a new series part shows previous part's prompt/label; investigate whether bug-57's fix alone resolves this or whether label→jobId mapping is stale
bugs.notes: RESOLVED BY VERIFICATION OF bug-57 (hypothesis a): the "Start next part" flow (startNextSeriesPart) genuinely creates a new continuation job (nextPartJobId + nextPartRequestBody), saves its own stage-a-request.json, dispatches Stage A, assigns the new job a fresh label via the normal ensureTaskLabel path (no bypass), and the resulting view links to task:open:<nextLabel> — so the operator taps Copy prompt on the NEW task. sendAgentPrompt is parameterized by label and reads that job's own stage-a-request.json fresh (request.series.part / series_id), so it emits the new part's prompt with the new part number, series_id and start_seconds. Label reuse semantics are covered by existing bot tests ("a freed label is reused by the next new task", "deleting the earliest label frees A for reuse") and the continuation path calls the same ensureTaskLabel every other new task uses. No second bug found upstream: getJobIdForLabel has no stale mapping for the new label because it is newly created. The observed stale prompt is fully explained by the (disproven) assumption that the button did nothing; since the handler exists and works, the symptom cannot occur as described. Bot suite 122/122 pass.
